title: temp_core temperature accuracy: full-signal-path mismatch Monte Carlo (PTAT/CTAT vs temperature) with per-term attribution
claim: Issue #105 -- NOT a spec claim and no spec/ edit (DR-003 row 2 stays [TBD-1]). Evidence toward TBD-1: the temperature error, in degC, of temp_core's PTAT output under local device mismatch over -40..125 C and the PVT corner matrix, reported untrimmed and with an ideal 1-point (27 C) gain trim, with the contribution of each mismatch term (PNP pair, amplifier offset, PTAT-gain resistor ratio, branch-current mirror, everything else) separated, plus an all-terms aggregate. The earlier sim/pnp-mismatch campaign (record 20260825-220116-a9cac4b) measured only the PNP DVBE term; this campaign adds the other terms and the aggregate.
statistical_convention: 3 sigma = 3 x the sample standard deviation (Bessel, n-1) of the temperature error over the valid Monte Carlo samples of ONE PVT corner (a +/-3 sigma half-width about the sample mean). Reported per corner, for the worst corner, and RMS-pooled over the 15 corners. Mean and empirical max |error| are tabulated alongside. Mismatch is local only (vary=mismatch); global process Monte Carlo (MC_PR_SWITCH) is not sampled.

error_definition.reference: same-corner no-mismatch run of the same deck (plain process section, no monte_carlo)
error_definition.volts_to_degC: divide by S = (V_nom(125 C) - V_nom(-40 C)) / 165 C, the nominal full-range slope of the same output at the same corner
error_definition.untrimmed: err(T) = (V_sample(T) - V_nom(T)) / S, evaluated at -40, 27, 125 C; headline = worst of the three
error_definition.trim_1point: PTAT: ideal multiplicative gain trim so V(27 C) equals nominal at 27 C; CTAT: additive offset trim at 27 C; error evaluated at -40 and 125 C (27 C is zero by construction). Trim resolution/quantization is not modelled.

provenance_source: design/netlist/{bias_core,temp_core}.spice (exported from design/*.sch); generated testbench in run_accuracy_mc.py

corners.temperature_note: swept inside each ngspice process (dc temp -40 125 1) so one Monte Carlo sample is one device realisation across temperature; a klt temperature corner axis would re-draw the realisation per temperature because klt derives the sample seed from the corner index

monte_carlo.execution: one klt sim request per (term, process section) = 3 supplies x N units, --backend batch (Spot fleet); never a local grid. Reason: a first attempt with one 3000-unit request per term hit the fleet per-job 1 h limit (batch_job_timeout, 3000/3000 errored; runner concurrency 1) and is disclosed in the record. Seed for process section k = seed + k (klt derives the sample seed from the corner index, which is 0..2 inside each request, so supplies share one realisation per process section and process sections draw independently).

terms.nominal: no mismatch; the per-corner reference curve
terms.none: negative control: _mm section + Monte Carlo with every device wrapped to sigma = 0; spread must be exactly zero
terms.other: all bias_core devices and every temp_core device not listed above
terms.all: every device has mismatch live (the aggregate)

operating_point_guards.scope: applied to EVERY sample at -40, 27 and 125 C; a failing sample is INVALID, excluded from the statistics, counted and disclosed, never trimmed or substituted
operating_point_guards.na_nb_T_spread_definition: branch consistency: max over T in {-40,27,125} C of |d(T) - median_T d|, d = V(NA)-V(NB). One device realisation keeps its amplifier offset across temperature (<= 0.32 mV spread on every on-branch sample of record 20261011-165400-69d13ac); a DC solution on another branch at a single temperature breaks loop closure there only. Added by the record that supersedes 20261011-165400-69d13ac (Judge review of PR #167).
operating_point_guards.offtrend_scan_degC: disclosure only, not a guard: 27 C PTAT error vs the chord through the -40/125 C errors; samples passing every guard but above 2 degC are listed in the record
operating_point_guards.windows_source: ptat/ctat/isup windows copied unchanged from sim/temp-core-startup-solver (#86); the NA/NB loop-closure, NA/NB branch-consistency and monotonic checks are specific to this DC-sweep bench
operating_point_guards.operating_point_trust: sim/temp-core-startup-solver/records/20261010-200708-47b96e5 (cited, not duplicated); its limits are inherited

measurement: dc sweep of temperature; .meas dc FIND v(ptat)/v(ctat)/v(xdut.na)/v(xdut.nb)/i(vsup) AT=-40/27/125
not_measured: systematic / gradient / layout-dependent mismatch, stress, aging, self-heating
dynamic behaviour (cold start, supply ramp): DC solutions only
physical trim ladder resolution and its mismatch
